cards.title: Crossing safely
facts: In India vehicles drive on the left, so traffic first comes from your right.
Many pedestrian accidents happen when people step out from between parked vehicles.
Phones and earphones hide traffic sounds.
do: Use zebra crossings, subways or footbridges
Stop at the kerb, look right, left and right again
Cross when the road is clear or vehicles have stopped
Walk, don't run, and keep looking
Hold a younger child's hand
dont: Don't cross between parked cars
Don't use your phone or earphones while crossing
Don't jump over road dividers

myths.statement: At a zebra crossing, all vehicles always stop, so you don't need to look.
myths.truth: Many drivers don't stop. Always look and make eye contact before crossing.

quiz.q: At a zebra crossing with no signal, what should you do before crossing?
options: Stop, look right, left and right again
Cross while looking at your phone
Wait for a friend to go first
quiz.explanation: Look both ways and cross only when it's clear or vehicles have stopped.

situations: After school, {name} and {relation} need to cross a busy road to reach {the}. The zebra crossing is 50 metres away, but there's a gap between two parked autos right in front of them.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Walk to the zebra crossing / safe crossing point
rubric.note: Crossings are where drivers expect you.

rubric.point: Don't cross between parked vehicles
rubric.note: Drivers can't see you step out.

rubric.point: Stop, look right-left-right and cross when clear
rubric.note: Traffic first comes from the right in India.

rubric.point: No phone or earphones; hold a younger child's hand

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: Helping at a road accident
facts: Moving an injured person can make a spine injury worse.
Removing a helmet can worsen a neck injury.
India's Good Samaritan rules protect people who help accident victims in good faith.
112 is India's single emergency number; 108 is the ambulance number in many states.
do: Make sure you are safe first
Warn traffic (hazard lights, warning triangle, a helper waving)
Call 112 or 108
Keep the injured person still and talk to them calmly
Stay until help arrives
dont: Don't move the injured person unless there is immediate danger like fire
Don't remove a helmet unless they can't breathe
Don't give food or water

myths.statement: If you help someone after an accident, the police will trouble you.
myths.truth: Good Samaritan rules protect people who help in good faith. You won't be forced to give personal details.

quiz.q: You're first to reach a bike accident on a busy road. The rider is awake but can't stand. What do you do first?
options: Lift them into a car and rush to hospital
Make the spot safe from traffic, then call 112
Take off their helmet so they can breathe
Give them water and help them sit up
quiz.explanation: Moving an injured person can make spine injuries worse, and a helmet should stay on unless they can't breathe. Make the scene safe, call 112, and stay with them. Good Samaritan rules protect people who help.

quiz.q: After a crash, a conscious biker is lying on the road. Should you take their helmet off?
options: Yes, right away so they can breathe
No. Leave it on unless they can't breathe
Only if they ask you to
Yes, then help them sit up
quiz.explanation: Removing a helmet can worsen a neck injury. Keep them still and call 112.

quiz.q: Which number works for any emergency in India?
quiz.explanation: 112 is India's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.

situations: {name} is the first to reach a bike accident on a busy road near {the}. The rider is awake but can't stand. {relation} wants to lift the rider into a car.
scenario.question: What should {name} do first?
scenario.bubble: Let's lift him into the car!

rubric.point: Make the scene safe and warn traffic
rubric.note: Protect yourself and the victim from other vehicles.

rubric.point: Don't move them or remove the helmet
rubric.note: Moving can worsen spine and neck injuries.

rubric.point: Stay with them and keep them calm

cards.title: Cycling safely
facts: Most cycling falls happen close to home on short rides.
A helmet only protects when it fits and the strap is fastened.
Riding with the flow of traffic makes you more visible and predictable.
do: Wear a helmet every ride, strap fastened
Ride on the left, with traffic
Use lights and reflectors at night
Use hand signals before turning
dont: Don't ride with earphones or a phone
Don't carry a friend on the carrier or crossbar
Don't ride against traffic

myths.statement: You only need a helmet on long rides or highways.
myths.truth: Most falls happen on short rides near home. Wear it every time.

quiz.q: When is a bicycle helmet most useful?
quiz.explanation: Wear it on every ride, strap fastened.

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: School bus safety
facts: Drivers of large vehicles have big blind spots right in front of and behind them.
Most bus-stop injuries happen while getting on or off.
do: Wait away from the road edge
Get on and off only when the bus has fully stopped
Keep hands and head inside
Cross only where the driver can see you, after the bus has moved
dont: Don't run after a moving bus
Don't jump off before it stops
Don't stand in the doorway

myths.statement: It's okay to jump off the bus just before it stops if you're careful.
myths.truth: Wait for a full stop. Moving vehicles throw you off balance.

quiz.q: Where is the safest place to get off a school bus?
options: Only at the stop, after the bus has fully stopped
From the back door in traffic
Jump off before it stops to save time
quiz.explanation: Wait for a full stop at the bus stop, then move away from the bus before crossing.

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: Saying NO to underage driving
facts: Driving without a valid licence is illegal under Section 199A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Parents and vehicle owners face heavy fines and imprisonment if a minor is caught driving.
do: Refuse politely and firmly if friends offer keys or pressure you to drive
Use public buses, cycles, or walk instead of unauthorized vehicles
Remind peers of legal penalties and accident risks
dont: Never drive a two-wheeler or car before age 18 (16 for gearless 50cc with licence)
Never accept rides from unlicensed minor peers

myths.statement: Driving inside a private colony without a licence is completely legal.
myths.truth: Motor Vehicle Act rules apply to all roads and public-access colonies.

quiz.q: A 14-year-old friend asks you to drive their father's scooter around the block. What should you do?
options: Firmly say NO and decline the keys
quiz.explanation: Underage driving is illegal, dangerous, and causes severe accidents.

situations: At {at}, a classmate shows car keys and invites {name} to go for a joyride.
scenario.question: What is the only responsible action for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Say NO firmly and refuse to ride or drive
Remind friend of legal penalties under MV Act
rubric.note: Awareness of 3-year jail for vehicle owner.

rubric.point: Choose safe walking or authorized transport

cards.title: Wearing seat belts in rear passenger seats
facts: Unbelted rear passengers become human missiles during a collision, crushing front occupants.
Wearing a seat belt reduces fatal collision injury rates by over 45%.
do: Fasten your three-point seat belt immediately upon entering any car
Adjust the lap belt snugly over hips and diagonal belt across chest
Remind fellow backseat passengers to buckle up before the car moves
dont: Never tuck the shoulder strap behind your back or armpit
Never share one seat belt between two people

myths.statement: Rear seat passengers do not need seat belts because front seats protect them.
myths.truth: Unbuckled rear passengers slam violently into front seats, killing front occupants.

quiz.q: Why is buckling up in the back seat just as critical as the front?
options: It stops you being launched forward into the front seats or windshield
quiz.explanation: In a crash, rear passengers fly forward at highway speed without belts.

situations: {name} gets into the rear seat of a taxi at {at} with {relation}.
scenario.question: What should {name} do before the taxi pulls into traffic?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Buckle the rear three-point seat belt securely
Position belt across collarbone and flat over hips
rubric.note: Distributes crash forces across strong bones.

rubric.point: Ask other family members to buckle up too

cards.title: Railway tracks and level crossing discipline
facts: High-speed trains require up to 1 kilometer of braking distance to stop completely.
Crossing closed railway barriers or walking along tracks is punishable under the Railway Act.
do: Wait patiently behind lowered crossing boom barriers until gates fully open
Cross tracks exclusively using Foot Over Bridges (FOBs) or subways
Remove headphones and look both directions at stations
dont: Never duck under or bypass closed level crossing gates
Never take photos, reels or walk along train tracks

myths.statement: You can easily see and hear an oncoming electric train from a mile away.
myths.truth: Modern electric locomotives produce minimal frontal noise until dangerously close.

quiz.q: A railway crossing gate is down and red signals are flashing. What is the rule?
options: Duck under if no train is visible
Wait behind the barrier until it lifts completely
quiz.explanation: Never bypass closed gates. Trains approach faster than they appear.

situations: On the way home from school at {at}, the railway crossing barrier lowers and warning bells ring.
scenario.question: What must {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Wait calmly behind the closed gate barrier
Do not duck under or follow impatient cyclists
rubric.note: Crossing closed gates is illegal and lethal.

rubric.point: Stay alert with headphones removed

cards.title: Metro and railway platform edge safety
facts: High-speed trains create an aerodynamic suction zone near the platform edge.
The yellow tactile strip marks the safety boundary away from moving trains.
do: Stand well behind the yellow safety line until the train comes to a complete halt
Allow arriving passengers to exit completely before boarding
Keep luggage, bags and feet behind the safety edge
dont: Never lean over the platform edge to look down the tracks
Never run on platforms or push in boarding lines

myths.statement: Standing right at the edge helps you get a seat faster without any danger.
myths.truth: Crowd surges or dizziness can cause instant falls onto high-voltage tracks.

quiz.q: What does the yellow tactile line on a metro or railway platform indicate?
options: The safety boundary: stay behind it until train stops
quiz.explanation: Standing behind the yellow line protects against suction and train collision.

situations: Waiting at the busy metro station at {at}, {name} sees people crowding the platform edge.
scenario.question: How should {name} position themselves safely?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stand firmly behind the yellow tactile safety line
rubric.note: Maintains safe standoff distance from tracks.

rubric.point: Allow alighting passengers to get off before boarding
Do not push, shove or run on the platform

sources.name: Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Safety Guide

cards.title: Never boarding or alighting from moving buses or trains
facts: Human foot speed cannot match vehicle momentum, throwing people under wheels.
Boarding or jumping from moving buses causes severe head trauma and wheel crushes.
do: Wait for the bus or auto to come to a full, stationary halt at the curb
Hold handrails firmly while stepping on or off
Queue in an orderly line at designated bus stops
dont: Never sprint to jump onto a moving bus footboard
Never lean out of doors or travel on the footboard

myths.statement: Jumping off a moving bus is safe if you run in the same direction.
myths.truth: Foot friction instantly flips the body backward under the rear dual wheels.

quiz.q: What must you always verify before stepping onto or off a bus?
options: That the vehicle has come to a complete, stationary stop
quiz.explanation: Never board or alight while tires are rotating.

situations: The school bus at {at} begins rolling forward while {name}'s friend tries to hop onto the footboard.
scenario.question: What should {name} tell their friend right now?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Wait and do not jump onto a moving vehicle
Signal the driver or conductor to stop fully
Never travel standing on the footboard

sources.name: State Transport Authority Road Safety Rules

cards.title: Navigating waterlogged roads and hidden manholes
facts: Rainwater conceals displaced manhole lids, deep potholes, and broken glass.
Fallen electric wires in pooled water conduct lethal currents across wide areas.
do: Avoid wading through deep or murky floodwater whenever possible
Stay on elevated pavements and test puddles with an umbrella stick
Keep clear of electric poles, junction boxes, and transformers
dont: Never step into swirling drain water
Never touch electric poles or lampposts in the rain

myths.statement: If others walk through waterlogged roads, it is safe to follow their steps.
myths.truth: Manhole covers get displaced in seconds by underground hydraulic pressure.

quiz.q: While walking home in heavy monsoon rains, the road ahead is flooded with brown water. What is the safest action?
options: Find a higher alternate route or seek shelter until water drains
quiz.explanation: Brown water hides open manholes and live electrical leaks.

situations: Sudden monsoon showers at {at} flood the road outside with knee-deep muddy water.
scenario.question: How should {name} proceed safely?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Avoid walking through murky floodwater; find higher dry ground
rubric.note: Hides missing manhole lids and open ditches.

rubric.point: Stay far away from electric poles and submerged transformers
Contact parents or wait with teachers in a sheltered shop

cards.title: Walking safely at night: Visibility and direction
facts: Drivers cannot spot pedestrians in dark clothing until they are under 18 meters away.
Walking facing oncoming traffic lets you see approaching headlights and react.
do: Wear light-coloured or reflective clothing after sunset
Walk on footpaths, or walk facing oncoming traffic if no footpath exists
Carry a flashlight or use mobile torch pointed at your feet
dont: Never walk in dark clothes with your back to vehicular traffic
Never cross unlit highway stretches without streetlights

myths.statement: Pedestrians can always be seen by car headlights from 100 meters away.
myths.truth: Low beams illuminate dark clothing only at very short, hazardous braking distances.

quiz.q: If there is no sidewalk on a rural or quiet road at night, which side should you walk on?
options: The left side with your back to cars
quiz.explanation: Facing oncoming traffic lets you see vehicle headlights and step off if needed.

situations: It's 8 PM at {at}. {name} needs to walk home along a road with broken streetlights.
scenario.question: How can {name} ensure maximum visibility and safety?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Wear light or reflective clothing and use a torch
rubric.note: Allows drivers to spot you from 100m away.

rubric.point: Walk facing oncoming traffic on the road shoulder
rubric.note: Maintains visual eye contact with approaching drivers.

rubric.point: Stay alert and avoid staring down at a mobile phone screen

cards.title: Speaking up against rash driving and speeding
facts: Over-speeding is responsible for over 70% of fatal road crashes in India.
Passengers have the legal right to demand the driver stop if they feel unsafe.
do: Speak up clearly and politely: 'Please slow down, I feel unsafe'
If the driver refuses, demand to be let off at a safe public spot
Call parents or 112 if in an auto or cab where driver refuses to stop
dont: Never stay quiet out of politeness or embarrassment
Never distract the driver by grabbing steering controls

myths.statement: Telling a driver to slow down makes them angry and drives worse.
myths.truth: A clear, calm passenger objection often snaps an overconfident driver out of aggressive driving.

quiz.q: You are in an auto-rickshaw that is overtaking rashly at dangerous speeds. What should you do?
options: Firmly request the driver to slow down or pull over
quiz.explanation: Voice your concern firmly and demand safe speed or exit at a safe spot.

situations: While traveling in a cab at {at}, the driver begins weaving through traffic at high speed.
scenario.question: What should {name} do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Politely and firmly ask driver: 'Please slow down, I do not want to speed'
If driver ignores, ask to pull over at the nearest well-lit public stop
rubric.note: Enables safe exit from dangerous vehicle.

rubric.point: Share live trip status with family or call 112 if threatened

cards.title: Witnessing a hit-and-run: Vital details and emergency report
facts: The first 60 seconds are critical for memorizing registration numbers and vehicle details.
Prompt medical dispatch during the Golden Hour saves 50% of crash victims.
do: Memorize registration number, vehicle color, model and direction of escape
Call 112 / 108 immediately and state exact accident location
Signal other bystanders to help create a safety perimeter around the victim
dont: Never chase a fleeing vehicle on foot or cycle
Never move an unconscious injured victim roughly

myths.statement: Witnesses should pursue hit-and-run drivers on their bicycles to catch them.
myths.truth: Chasing fleeing vehicles leads to secondary crashes. Memorize details and call police.

quiz.q: You witness a car hit a cyclist and speed away. What is the most critical information to note?
options: The car's license plate number, color, and make
quiz.explanation: Vehicle registration number enables police to apprehend the fleeing driver.

situations: At {at}, a speeding car hits a pedestrian and flees without stopping.
scenario.question: What key actions should {name} take immediately?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Note registration number, vehicle make, color, and direction
Call 112 for police and 108 for ambulance immediately
Stay at a safe distance and help comfort the injured person

sources.name: Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety

cards.title: Staying out of truck and bus blind spots (No-Zones)
facts: Heavy trucks have massive blind spots directly in front, directly behind, and along both flanks.
If you cannot see the truck driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.
do: Maintain at least 10 meters distance when following behind large buses or trucks
Never overtake a truck on the left (curb) side when it might turn
Pass trucks briskly on the right without lingering in their side blind spots
dont: Never squeeze your cycle between a turning truck and the curb
Never tailgate directly behind container trucks

myths.statement: Truck drivers have elevated seats so they can see everything right around their bumper.
myths.truth: High bonnets create a 6-meter blind zone directly in front where small pedestrians are invisible.

quiz.q: What is the golden rule of heavy vehicle mirrors?
options: If you cannot see the driver in their mirror, they cannot see you
quiz.explanation: If the mirror doesn't reflect the driver's eyes, you are in their blind spot.

situations: Riding a bicycle at {at}, {name} approaches a large cement truck that is signaling a left turn.
scenario.question: What is the only safe move for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stay well behind the truck and do not squeeze on the left side
rubric.note: Left turns create deadly rear-wheel pinch zones.

rubric.point: Keep visual contact with driver's right mirror
rubric.note: Ensures driver is aware of presence.

rubric.point: Give the truck plenty of turning room

cards.title: Headphones, phones and audio awareness near traffic
facts: Audio cues (horns, engine revs, tire screeches) provide 50% of pedestrian hazard warnings.
Active noise cancellation completely blocks ambient sounds of approaching electric vehicles.
do: Keep one ear completely uncovered or turn off noise-cancellation near roadways
Pause music and pocket phones before stepping off curbs to cross
Look left-right-left even when music is off
dont: Never walk across busy intersections while texting or browsing
Never wear over-ear headphones at maximum volume on roads

myths.statement: Looking with your eyes is enough; hearing plays no role in pedestrian safety.
myths.truth: Auditory cues detect vehicles turning from behind and speeding in blind corners.

quiz.q: Why is wearing noise-cancelling headphones while walking near roads dangerous?
options: It blocks horns and approaching engine noises, preventing evasion
quiz.explanation: Blocked hearing prevents you from reacting to horns and approaching sirens.

situations: Walking toward school along a busy road at {at}, {name}'s friend has big headphones playing loud music.
scenario.question: What should {name} advise their friend?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Take off headphones or keep one ear free near traffic
rubric.keys: take off headphones|one ear free|volume down

rubric.point: Stay fully alert to vehicle horns, reversing beeps and sirens
Keep phone inside bag rather than texting while walking

cards.title: Handling stray dogs barking or chasing your cycle
facts: Dogs have an innate predatory chase instinct triggered by fast spinning pedals and panic.
Panic pedaling causes cyclists to swerve into oncoming cars and crash.
do: Stop pedaling, slow down smoothly, and dismount calmly
Place the bicycle between yourself and the dog as a physical barrier
Speak firmly in a low, calm voice: 'No! Go home!' without shouting
dont: Never pedal faster in blind panic into traffic
Never kick out with your feet, which risks severe bites and falls

myths.statement: Pedaling as hard as possible is the best way to outrun a street dog.
myths.truth: Chasing speeds up dogs and causes cyclists to crash into curbs or vehicles.

quiz.q: A stray street dog begins barking and chasing your bicycle. What should you do?
options: Pedal wildly into the main road
Slow down steadily, dismount, and keep cycle between you and dog
quiz.explanation: Dismounting cancels the chase reflex and the bicycle frame acts as a shield.

situations: Cycling down a colony lane at {at}, two street dogs run out barking loudly at {name}'s tires.
scenario.question: How should {name} handle this safely?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Slow down steadily without swerving into traffic
Dismount and keep the bicycle frame between self and dogs
rubric.note: Forms a sturdy physical defensive shield.

rubric.point: Walk calmly away without running or making eye contact

cards.title: Essential road signs every student must recognize
facts: Circular signs with red borders give orders (prohibitions); triangular signs give warnings.
School Zone signs indicate 25 km/h limits and high pedestrian crossing density.
do: Recognize octagonal red STOP signs (must come to complete halt)
Recognize triangular Pedestrian Crossing and School Ahead warning signs
Follow blue circular signs which indicate compulsory positive instructions
dont: Never ignore 'No Entry' or 'One Way' street markings
Never cross against red pedestrian walking figures

myths.statement: School zone signs are only meant for bus drivers, not cyclists or pedestrians.
myths.truth: Traffic signs govern all road users, helping cyclists predict driver behaviors.

quiz.q: What shape is an international regulatory STOP sign on Indian roads?
quiz.explanation: The octagonal shape is unique so drivers can recognize it even when covered in snow or mud.

situations: At the intersection outside school at {at}, {name} sees an octagonal red sign and a pedestrian crossing symbol.
scenario.question: What do these signs instruct road users to do?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: STOP requires vehicles to come to a full stationary halt
Pedestrian crossing warns of designated walking rights-of-way
Check all directions before stepping onto zebra lines

sources.name: Indian Roads Congress (IRC) Traffic Sign Code

cards.title: Calling emergency services: Being an effective crash witness
facts: Clear landmark descriptions allow ambulance dispatchers to reach victims 10 minutes faster.
Panicking and hanging up delays medical intervention during trauma care.
do: State the exact location first (road name, nearest shop/landmark, intersection)
State the number of injured persons and whether anyone is trapped or unconscious
Stay on the call until the emergency operator instructs you to hang up
dont: Never give vague directions like 'near a big tree'
Never hang up before the dispatcher confirms location

myths.statement: When calling 112/108, describing the injuries is more important than giving the location.
myths.truth: If the call drops before location is known, help cannot be dispatched.

quiz.q: What is the first thing you must clearly tell the 112/108 emergency operator?
options: The exact location with a prominent landmark
quiz.explanation: Location first allows operators to dispatch the nearest emergency unit while you talk.

situations: {name} comes across a two-wheeler collision at {at} and dials 112.
scenario.question: How should {name} structure the emergency report?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Provide exact road name and prominent nearby landmark first
Report number of injured persons and conscious state
Stay on the line and follow dispatcher instructions

sources.name: National Emergency Response Support System (112 India)

cards.title: Good Samaritan protections under Indian law
facts: The Supreme Court of India established Good Samaritan rules to protect crash helpers from harassment.
Hospitals cannot force Good Samaritans to pay admission fees or reveal personal identities.
do: Help accident victims without fear of legal or police harassment
Good Samaritans can leave immediately after taking a victim to hospital
You are not required to become a court witness unless you voluntarily choose to
dont: Never withhold help because of fear of police questioning
Never take photos of victims instead of rendering aid

myths.statement: If you help a road accident victim into an ambulance, police will force you to pay for hospital care.
myths.truth: Under Indian Good Samaritan law, helpers cannot be forced to pay or face detention.

quiz.q: What legal protection does the Indian Good Samaritan law grant citizens who help accident victims?
options: Complete immunity from police harassment, detention, and hospital fee liability
quiz.explanation: Good Samaritans are legally protected to encourage life-saving bystander intervention.

situations: A road crash occurs at {at}. Bystanders are hesitant to help, fearing police harassment.
scenario.question: What should {name} explain to encourage safe bystander assistance?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Indian Good Samaritan law protects helpers from police interrogation
Helpers cannot be forced to pay hospital admission charges
rubric.note: Hospitals are legally required to accept trauma victims.

rubric.point: Calling 108 and comforting the injured saves lives during the Golden Hour

sources.name: Ministry of Road Transport Good Samaritan Guidelines
